title: Doc Advisor routes broad subsystem lore to a system spec
query: Our feature page for a docs capability has grown into broad policy for where all docs live, how feature and system specs work, and how generated registries are maintained. Some of that policy also got copied into docs skill references, and I am not sure what should live where or what checks prove the split. How should we reshape it?
reference_points: Recognizes that broad documentation governance is system-shaped rather than only a single feature slice
Recommends a system spec such as Documentation OS for product-layer boundaries and long-lived documentation architecture
Keeps the feature doc as a narrower capability slice with behavior, surfaces, proof, limits, and maintenance path
Explains why a skill reference should own executable branch workflow rather than canonical lore
Names registry validation or doc reference checks as proof after moving the boundary
notes: Covers the FEAT-0060 promotion failure mode that triggered the Documentation OS split.

title: Doc Advisor loads branch references instead of bloating first load
query: I need to update a system spec and a feature page, but I am not sure what front matter and registry sync rules apply. What should the documentation workflow do first?
reference_points: Binds the reader, target surfaces, source of truth, and proof route before editing
Loads the metadata/registry branch reference because front matter and generated registries are in scope
Loads the feature/system spec branch reference because both FEAT and SYS boundaries are in scope
Does not expand every documentation architecture rule into the first-load workflow
Names generated registries as outputs and says not to hand-edit JSONL rows
notes: Protects the method-reference split and template 0.3.6 progressive disclosure behavior.

title: Doc Advisor finish gate preserves repair context over scalar scores
query: I finished a durable docs cleanup. Can we summarize it with a doc quality score and ship if the number is high?
reference_points: Rejects using a scalar documentation quality score as readiness proof
Treats the QA checklist as inspection evidence with failed checks, fixes, deferrals, and remaining risk
Routes material readiness to documentation-quality review when a TAS verdict is needed
Preserves reasons and repair hints instead of collapsing feedback into a number
Names relevant validators or focused searches only when they match the changed doc surface
notes: Protects the quality signal boundary introduced after the metrics/rubric/checklist discussion.

title: Doc Advisor returns a compact no-docs strategy
query: I am planning a material ticket that only renames an internal test fixture and does not touch README, feature specs, user docs, or public workflow behavior. What docs section should the ticket carry?
reference_points: Returns a Docs Strategy block rather than a Documentation / Closeout block
Uses outcome no_docs when no durable docs should change
Includes a concrete no_docs_reason tied to the absence of public, canonical, or workflow-facing doc changes
Does not add close_ticket or documentation_skill fields
Names validation such as focused grep, tests, or no public surface touched
notes: Protects TASK-0241's docs strategy contract and prevents closeout ceremony from returning.
